items.title: Real CV intake
items.goal: Real CVs reach the portal through recruiter upload, an intake mailbox, and a one-time OneDrive or SharePoint import of files changed in the last 12 months — each through the same parser the MVP proved.
prd: CV processing → Intake: recruiter upload (drag and drop, one file or many); email inbox with the mailbox chosen later; one-time OneDrive / SharePoint import of files changed in the last 12 months → decided for the real-data release
Integrations → intake mailbox address and OneDrive folders are still to decide → open
Data, privacy & compliance → Risk 2 (resolved): only files changed in the last 12 months are imported, with consent recorded per imported candidate → decided
exit: This epic is a stub. It is planned in detail only after the MVP go/no-go decision
Its entry conditions are the real-data prerequisites recorded in the go/no-go pack
outOfScope: Everything, until the go/no-go decision is made. Nothing here is scheduled
Sending email: the portal receives CVs by email but never sends any

items.title: Consent, retention & data subject rights
items.goal: PDPA obligations are enforced in the product: recorded consent with a dashboard reminder after 7 days and deletion after 14 without it, 12-month retention from last activity with a warning 30 days before, candidates without consent hidden from search and matching, plus export and correction on request and logging good enough to assess a breach's scope.
prd: Data, privacy & compliance → Consent: recorded by phone or the recruiter's own email with date and method; dashboard reminder after 7 days; CV deleted after 14 days without consent; non-consented candidates hidden from search and matching → decided
Data, privacy & compliance → Retention: delete or anonymise 12 months after last activity, with a warning 30 days before (warning proposed) → decided
Data, privacy & compliance → Access & correction: recruiters can export or correct a candidate's data on request → proposed
Data, privacy & compliance → Breach notification: log access and changes so a breach's scope can be assessed; 500 or more people must be reported to PDPC within 3 calendar days → proposed
Talent search → requirement 5: candidates without consent or past retention are hidden → proposed
exit: This epic is a stub. It is planned in detail only after the MVP go/no-go decision
No consent or retention behaviour is built while the MVP holds fictional data only
outOfScope: Everything, until the go/no-go decision is made
Sending consent requests by email — the portal never sends email; reminders appear on the dashboard

items.title: Access protection before real data
items.goal: Before a single real CV is loaded, the portal stops being readable by anyone with the link — through sign-in (Microsoft 365 via Supabase Auth fits the agency's setup) or office-network-only access — with access logged.
prd: Users → whether sign-in is required before real CVs are loaded → open

Data, privacy & compliance → Risk 1: with no sign-in anyone who finds the address could see every CV; loading real CVs that way would breach PDPA's Protection Obligation, with fines up to S$1 million or 10% of Singapore turnover → decided as a risk, accepted for fictional data only
Security (suggested) → when sign-in is added, Supabase Auth with Microsoft sign-in fits the agency's Microsoft 365 setup; Vercel Pro password protection costs $20 a month → suggested
Open questions → what must be in place before real CVs are loaded: sign-in, consent recording, the retention job, a legal review? No owner named → open
exit: This epic is a stub. It is planned in detail only after the MVP go/no-go decision
It is the hardest prerequisite for real data: nothing in the real-data release starts before this is decided
outOfScope: Everything, until the go/no-go decision is made
Adding sign-in to the MVP — the PRD explicitly accepts its absence for fictional data

items.title: Duplicate candidates
items.goal: Resubmissions and re-imports of the same person are recognised under a rule the product owner sets after the go/no-go decision, instead of becoming separate candidates as they do in the MVP.
prd: CV processing → requirement 4: duplicate detection is left out of the MVP and its rule must be decided before real data → proposed / open
Non-goals → duplicate candidate detection is out of the MVP
Open questions → the rule for spotting duplicate candidates, decided after the MVP go/no-go → open
Sample data → resubmissions exist in the sample set and are logged for this decision
exit: This epic is a stub. It is planned in detail only after the rule is decided
The likely resubmissions the MVP seed logs are the starting evidence for that decision
outOfScope: Everything, until the rule is decided
Merging candidates in the MVP — an explicit non-goal

items.title: Paid plans & backups
items.goal: The portal moves off free tiers before recruiters use it for real work — Vercel Pro because Hobby forbids commercial use, and a paid Supabase tier with a backup policy — sized for under 1,000 CVs a month.
prd: Free-tier limits → Vercel Hobby is for non-commercial use only; move to Pro before recruiters use the portal for real work → decided
Free-tier limits → Supabase Free has no backups and pauses after a week idle; 500 MB database, 1 GB storage, 50 MB per file → decided
Non-functional requirements → Backups: none in the MVP; needed before real data → decided
Non-functional requirements → Scale after real data: under 1,000 CVs per month, 6–20 recruiters → decided
Open questions → which paid plans to move to; how backups work and how long they are kept → open
exit: This epic is a stub. It is planned in detail only after the plan and backup decisions are made
Both decisions are open questions recorded in the register
outOfScope: Everything, until the plan and backup decisions are made
Using Vercel Hobby for real agency work — that would breach Vercel's terms
